data.body: Diagnosis: live session in master_feedback showed Electron renderer at ~147% CPU and ~709 MB RSS while audio service was idle. Most likely crackles/dropouts are audio starvation from renderer load/GC. Primary code suspects: SpectralHistoryPanel copies and reprocesses up to 7200 PSD snapshots every metrics batch/render; master_feedback always mounts it; master_feedback also runs up to 7 AudioScene media-element loop pairs and schedules gain ramps for each metric update; backend/session recorder stores raw rows, PSD rows, and program outputs in memory until stop/save, adding long-session pressure. Immediate workaround: lower broadcast rate to 1 Hz and/or navigate away/hide heavy spectral history during training; proper fix is throttle/virtualize/downsample spectral history, avoid whole-history recompute, and stream session recording to disk.

Completed diagnostic only; no app code changed. Reviewed live backend state, process CPU/memory, frontend audio scene, master feedback view, WebSocket cadence, spectral history rendering, and recorder memory behavior. Finding: the active master_feedback Electron renderer was pegged (~147% CPU, ~709 MB RSS) while audio service was idle, pointing to renderer starvation/GC as the likely source of long-session cracks/dropouts. Primary culprit is SpectralHistoryPanel whole-history copy/rebin/redraw work plus master_feedback always mounting it; secondary contributors are multiple simultaneous AudioScene media elements/ramp scheduling and backend in-memory session accumulation. Recommended fixes: throttle/downsample/workerize spectral history, cap visible PSD history by time/window, skip expensive panels while training unless expanded, coalesce audio parameter updates, and stream recorder data to disk.
